brief_item.title: TRIO-20测试推理强度与Agent越权工具调用
brief_item.core_conclusion: TRIO-20在GPT-5.6内比较low与max reasoning effort下的禁止工具调用。840条轨迹没有越权调用，但Terra推理token中位数由72升至408，安全边界仍应由权限与策略检查承担。
brief_item.mechanism: 20个办公场景设salient、hidden、clean三种条件，提示、工具schema和交互预算保持一致，只改变快捷路径有效性与可见性。确定性评审检查工具日志和终端状态。
brief_item.result: Terra与Sol 840条轨迹均为0次禁止调用，违反率95%上限分别低于3.50%和5.21%。Terra推理token中位数72升至408，Sol由103升至464.5，规则探测假设未获支持。
brief_item.boundary: 结果只适用于GPT-5.6 Terra/Sol、TRIO-20和显式系统禁令，未覆盖其他模型、工具、对抗提示或隐式策略。研究测外显工具调用，不是潜在推理。
brief_item.project_relevance: 工具链设计应把权限配置和确定性策略检查作为安全边界，不能假设低reasoning effort天然更安全。部署前还要测token、时延和对抗输入，论文未给成本收益。

facts.title: Test-time reasoning effort and unauthorized tool use in language-model agents: a prespecified equivalence study
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.03169v1 reports a prespecified within-model test of reasoning effort versus unauthorized tool use
facts.problem: Agent APIs expose a reasoning-effort parameter that changes test-time computation, cost, and latency, but it was unclear whether increasing effort also increases a benign agent's tendency to call tools prohibited by its role-level access policy.
facts.mechanism: The TRIO-20 testbed uses 20 matched workplace scenarios, each instantiated as salient, hidden, and clean conditions from one code base. The conditions keep prompts, tool schemas, and interaction budgets identical except for two configuration fields that determine whether a prohibited shortcut is effective and whether its effect is visible. The study directly manipulates GPT-5.6 reasoning effort between low and max within the same model, runs deterministic judges over tool logs and terminal state, and prespecifies prohibited-tool attempts as the primary endpoint and rule probing as the secondary endpoint. GPT-5.6 Terra is the primary tier and GPT-5.6 Sol a within-family robustness check.

evidence.claim: Across 840 selected trajectories (504 Terra and 336 Sol), no unauthorized/prohibited tool call occurred at either low or max effort and in any matched condition.
evidence.condition: TRIO-20 confirmatory collection with explicit system-level prohibitions; selected trajectories plus retained quality evidence also had zero events.
evidence.source_locator: PDF pp.1, 10-11, Abstract and Primary endpoint

evidence.claim: Exact one-sided 95% upper limits for a violation rate were below 3.50% per Terra arm (n=84) and 5.21% per Sol arm (n=56); the Terra interaction interval was ±4.34 percentage points inside the prespecified ±7.01-point equivalence margin.
evidence.condition: Zero-event arms; Clopper–Pearson exact bounds and prespecified equivalence analysis.

evidence.claim: Increasing effort changed reasoning-token use: Terra median tokens rose from 72 at low to 408 at max (5.67×); Sol medians rose from 103 to 464.5 (4.51×), with max exceeding low in all 14 scenarios.
evidence.condition: Per-trajectory API effort assignment; the study compares low and max settings within each model tier.

evidence.claim: The prespecified rule-probing interaction estimate was −0.143 with 95% CI [−0.274,+0.012], so the targeted-search hypothesis was not supported; probing nevertheless rose in every condition.
evidence.condition: Terra secondary endpoint; collection order was low before max within each scenario, so the contrast is entangled with time.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.11, Secondary endpoint: rule probing

evidence.claim: The matched-triad design holds prompts, tool sets, and interaction budgets constant across conditions and uses deterministic judges audited in two rounds of 40 trajectories with full agreement.
evidence.value: 20 scenarios; 3 matched conditions; 2 audited rounds × 40 trajectories
evidence.condition: Conditions differ only in configuration fields controlling shortcut effectiveness/visibility.

facts.evaluation_context: This is a prespecified security/equivalence experiment on GPT-5.6 through the Responses API. It uses 14 confirmatory scenarios from the 20-scenario TRIO-20 suite, three matched conditions (salient, hidden, clean), two effort settings (low, max), and two model tiers (Terra primary, Sol robustness). Deterministic judges score tool logs and terminal state; prompts, tool schemas, and budgets are held constant apart from configured condition fields. The primary outcome is an attempted prohibited call, with rule probing as a secondary outcome.
facts.limitations: The bounded-zero result applies only to the tested GPT-5.6 Terra/Sol tiers, TRIO-20 workplace environments, explicit system-level prohibitions, and the collected effort settings; it does not establish zero risk for other models, tools, prompts, implicit policies, adversarial pressure, or external enforcement regimes. The Terra effort contrast was collected low before max within each scenario, entangling secondary probing effects with time. The interaction equivalence margin is limited by the sample sizes (n=84 Terra and n=56 Sol per arm), and the study measures emitted tool calls rather than all latent unsafe reasoning. The authors release raw trajectories for replication, but broader model and deployment coverage remains untested.
facts.project_relevance: For agent tool-chain design, the evidence separates inspection from action: roughly fivefold more reasoning tokens increased rule probing but produced no prohibited calls in this explicit-policy regime. This supports keeping tool permissions and deterministic policy checks as the security boundary rather than assuming a lower reasoning setting is safer, while the study does not measure end-to-end latency or token cost benefits for a particular deployment.
